body.x: MAKEMAKE (CEO Hyoseob Kwak) participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ held on July 30. Organizers arranged this meetup to inform overseas media about participating companies’ products and technologies in advance for global markets while expanding business opportunities. MAKEMAKE is a chemical-based beauty-tech startup solving problems water leaves on skin and hair through material technology. It will unveil its new non-powered portable soft water tumbler ‘PERLUO’ for the first time at CES in January 2027. CEO Hyoseob Kwak delivered the presentation on this day.

It started with swimming. Swimming pool water contains chloramines (residual chlorine) formed by combining chlorine with body secretions, which regular shampoos fail to remove effectively, and products caring for scalp and hair after swimming were non-existent. MAKEMAKE resolved this issue with its self-developed zeolite composite material technology, ‘ZeoDualite™’. According to the company, this material removes up to 98% of residual chlorine based on external evaluations. In October 2024, the company first introduced ‘SOOO’, a swim-exclusive shampoo brand applying this material. In July 2025, the company completed patent registration for ZeoDualite™.

body.cap: App screen of MAKEMAKE’s non-powered portable soft water tumbler ‘PERLUO’ | Provided by MAKEMAKE

body.x: Established in May 2024, MAKEMAKE formed its team with CEO Hyoseob Kwak—boasting e-commerce and beauty new business experience—alongside a technical lead holding a Ph.D. in chemistry and experience at EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, Switzerland), and a creative lead who won all three of the world’s top design awards (Red Dot, iF, IDEA). Featuring a full-stack structure that places front-end capabilities in planning, branding, marketing, global expansion, and operations alongside back-end capabilities in R&D, research infrastructure, and manufacturing know-how within a single company, the company promotes its strength in maintaining short development cycles without outsourcing, reflecting market signals directly into material development.

PERLUO, unveiled for the first time at CES, represents the first product expanding from swimming pool care to ‘water stress care’. When users pour tap water, insert a replaceable cartridge, and shake for about 60 seconds, water repeatedly passes through the cartridge material, filtering out hardness components (calcium, magnesium) and trace metals originating from aging pipes. The porous framework captures calcium and magnesium, while chelating functional groups bind metals. Requiring no pumps, piping, or external power, users can operate it identically at home, hotels, or gyms, while repeatedly using the main body and replacing cartridges to drive recurring subscription re-orders. MAKEMAKE aims to address water environment-specific issues—such as residual chlorine, hard water minerals, heavy metals from aging pipes, and seawater salinity—with respective dedicated materials.

body.cap: MAKEMAKE CEO Hyoseob Kwak (left) during an interview with Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Achievements accumulate continuously as well. SOOO entered major channels including domestic Health & Beauty (H&B) stores, department store pop-ups, major messenger gifting platforms, and in-flight duty-free shops, with company mall membership exceeding 20,000 members. Collaborations on luxury hotel amenities and official sponsorships of national swimming competitions progress in parallel. Overseas, the company opened an official brand store on Amazon North America, maintaining a 4.8 rating for its children’s swim-care products, while completing US trademark registration and FDA approvals. With a Brazilian distributor, the company achieved an initial export of 100,000 USD with chelating products designed to remove heavy metals from aging pipes, while earning adoption in Turkish premium salons and UAE luxury hotels. In November 2025, the company won the Grand Prize in the Haircare category at Asia’s largest beauty exhibition, and in January 2026, earned the Grand Prize at the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ ‘K-Beauty in Shanghai’.

Financial performance grew from 5 billion KRW in revenue in 2025 (500 million KRW in exports) to 5.8 billion KRW in the first half of 2026, targeting 12 billion KRW annually. In terms of investment, seed funding attraction was followed by selections for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups TIPS and IBK Changgong 15th batch. MAKEMAKE plans sequential expansion into Europe, South America, and Japan led by Amazon North America, internalizing material development and validation centered around its corporate research institute established in January 2026. Commercialization of hair loss alleviation technology based on Viola mandshurica extract transferred from a research institution under the Ministry of Environment is in preparation as well.

body.cap: Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen (left) and MAKEMAKE CEO Hyoseob Kwak take a commemorative photo after concluding the Global Media Meetup. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Hyoseob Kwak, CEO of MAKEMAKE, stated, “Water stress is not severe in Korea because tap water is soft, but hair and skin damage from minerals and heavy metals runs far more serious in the US, Europe, and South America.” He added, “Residual chlorine, minerals, heavy metals, and salinity ultimately stem from a single problem rooted in water, and we will solve this comprehensively through material technology.” He continued, saying, “We will demonstrate that K-beauty possesses competitiveness not only in formulations and marketing but also in core material technologies, growing from swimming pools into a brand managing all water-induced issues.”
